caseAnalysis.title: Camp Alpha Commander and FWB food distribution negotiation
caseAnalysis.summary: The Camp Commander of Alpha's largest refugee camp (160,000 refugees, about 700 guards) is approached by an FWB negotiator. The role card says the commander keeps underpaid guards partly with refugee food stocks and fears guard rebellion. He sees independent FWB distribution and FWB-hired local laborers as threats to his authority. It describes an agreement that includes ongoing food aid as highly attractive. Confiscating the food would risk an international incident and the end of all future aid. In an earlier meeting, FWB reportedly refused to feed guards on neutrality grounds, insisted on FWB-managed distribution and requested nutritional assessments for a donor requirement. The camp side insisted on distribution through guard structures and escorted FWB presence. SML transcripts add demands for paid militia involvement, plus statements about skimming and unequal distribution. Officials warn that unrest or visible abuse would be politically costly.
caseAnalysis.objective: Reach an agreement with FWB, preferably including ongoing food aid, that helps sustain guards and keeps refugees in the camp while preserving camp stability and the commander's authority, and avoids major unrest or visible abuse.

issues.text: Guard compensation through food conflicts with FWB's reported refusal to feed guards. The role card says guards may rebel if they see refugees eating better than they are.
Distribution control is contested. The camp side wants distribution through guard structures. FWB insists on FWB-managed disbursement, potentially with FWB-chosen local assistants.
SML statements about skimming food, distributing it unequally and implicitly threatening FWB conflict with officials' warning that visible abuse would be politically costly.
The basis of FWB's nutritional assessment request (a donor requirement) is reported and doubted by the camp side, so it is unverified.
The role card states no explicit hard red lines or formal authority limits for the commander. SML's demands are third-party positions, not our constraints.

immediate.text: Per the role card, a new FWB negotiator has reached out to the commander. A prior meeting ended with FWB refusing to feed guards and both sides insisting on control of distribution.

actors.text: The Camp Commander (our side) commands about 700 guards for 160,000 refugees. He has been retaining guards partly with refugee food stocks.
FWB, as reported in the minutes, will not feed guards and insists on managing disbursement itself.
SML demands that militia men be involved in distribution and be compensated properly, and that this be settled before FWB arrives.
The Mayor's Office wants camp-linked local jobs and income protected and local actors prioritized, and says tensions cannot be allowed to escalate.

Alpha officials reportedly warned that major unrest or visible abuse drawing international attention would be politically costly. The government is counting on the commander to keep refugees from swamping the capital.
MASHA has a working relationship with the camp side. Its access and notes clear through Camp Admin's office.

tension.text: The role card says FWB food would help pay guards and keep refugees in the camp. It also says independent FWB distribution may undermine the commander's authority, and that FWB refuses to feed guards.

background.text: The role card attributes guard pay problems to government corruption. Some refugees trade rations, which are resold locally. CC says the generator is failing and the petrol company has not been paid for weeks.

uncertainty.text: Whether FWB's assessment request really reflects a donor requirement; the minutes say it 'may be true'.
SML's instruction to 'take the food' is ambiguous between accepting the aid and seizing it.
No food quantities, duration of aid or FWB delivery date are documented.

response_branches.text: If FWB reiterates it will not feed guards, acknowledge its neutrality stance. Ask whether non-food support for camp operations is within its mandate, without assuming it is.
If FWB insists on managing disbursement, discuss escort and coordination arrangements. The camp side has stated that unrestricted movement is unacceptable under current conditions.
If FWB presses for assessments, discuss security-safe timing and modality, given the camp side's concern that delays could raise tensions.

critical_assumptions.text: Assumes FWB is open to ongoing aid; this is not documented.
Assumes guard stability can be addressed without diverting refugee food. Officials warn that visible abuse is politically costly.
Assumes SML will accept a negotiated arrangement short of his demands; this is not documented.

negotiation_issues.title: FWB access and escort in camp

counterpart_position.text: FWB says it needs access to distribute food.

background.text: The commander previously served in the militia on the Omega border. Refugees fled unrest in Omega after a failed coup.
The incident log records notes proposing coordinated refusal of camp orders.

people_interests_power.text: CC fears SML would send a hitman if SML thinks CC is going to crack.
The Mayor's Office expects local actors to be prioritized in camp activities.

pressures_disagreements.text: The petrol supplier agreed to send the truck tomorrow after CC asked for one more week; SML's payment is promised for next week.
CC proposed an implicit threat to FWB's safety; SML conditionally endorsed it.

no_agreement_consequences.text: Without agreement, guard discipline may deteriorate and food shortages persist. CC says that if staff cannot feed themselves, no one will feed the prisoners.

team_questions.text: What authority does SML hold over the deal, and is government approval needed?

counterpart_questions.text: What are FWB's minimum monitoring and donor requirements?
